cases.prompt: I'm adding username/password login to my Express API. I was going to sign a JWT and save it in localStorage on the client. Can you implement the auth flow?
expectations: Rejects storing the JWT in localStorage and explains it is vulnerable to XSS, recommending httpOnly cookies instead
Hashes passwords with bcrypt or argon2 rather than storing plain passwords
Sets short-lived access tokens of 15-30 minutes maximum
Sets secure cookie flags (httpOnly, secure, sameSite)
Validates input server-side (email format, password strength) rather than trusting client data
Adds rate limiting on the auth endpoints to prevent brute-force attacks

cases.prompt: How should I decide what each logged-in user is allowed to do? I have admins, editors, and regular users.
expectations: Distinguishes authorization (what you can do) from authentication (who you are)
Describes role-based access control (RBAC) for the admin/editor/user roles
Includes resource ownership validation in addition to role checks
Emphasizes that permission checks must be enforced server-side, not only in client code
Warns against trusting client-provided role or permission data

cases.prompt: Can you add a 'Sign in with Google' button to our app?
expectations: Frames this as OAuth2/OpenID Connect delegated authentication
Mentions validating the identity token/claims on the server rather than trusting the client
Notes short-lived access tokens and token expiration
Keeps secrets/server credentials on the backend and out of client code

cases.prompt: We need a forgot-password flow that emails the user a reset link. What's the secure way to build it?
expectations: Uses secure, single-use reset tokens with an expiration rather than guessing user identity
Avoids user enumeration, so the response is the same whether or not the email exists
Rate limits password reset requests to prevent abuse
Hashes the new password with bcrypt/argon2 before storing it

cases.prompt: Our API is broken because the frontend reportedly hides the admin button from non-admins, but someone still hit the admin endpoint directly and it worked. Why, and how do we fix it?
expectations: Identifies that client-side auth checks alone are insufficient
States that authorization must always be validated on the server
Recommends enforcing the permission check in the API/route handler for the admin endpoint
References logging security events such as failed or unauthorized access attempts
